packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-16 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted, no identification attempted)

Exposure note: none. Only the images and PROMPT.md of this packet were read.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 and image-005 are overviews of the two sides of one upright parchment leaf (colour
  target at right; a paper tab at one upper corner; an oval hole near the inner/outer margin).
- Each side: ONE column of verse, one verse per ruled line, 33 lines, in a gothic bookhand,
  dark brown ink. The lines rhyme in pairs (end-rhyme, often also internal rhyme). Each line
  begins with a slightly offset capital; red paragraph marks ("§"-like strokes) stand in the
  left margin at intervals of about two lines.
- Enlarged 2-line pen initials mark new sections: "V" (side 1, line 15), "S" (side 1, line 21),
  "C" (side 2, line 10, mostly hidden by a stain/patch), "P" (side 2, line 22), "Q" (side 2,
  line 32). Beside each stands a red rubric in the margin (left margin on side 1, right margin
  on side 2), partly cut by the leaf edge.
- Glosses: short interlinear glosses in a small lighter hand (e.g. "symonie", "ordinem", "etiam")
  and marginal glosses in the same small hand, several of them legal-style citations
  (".i. q. i. Sunt nonnulli", "Extra ... e. Mandato"). On side 2 the left margin also has cut
  glosses, and a strip/patch of another parchment (binding reinforcement) is pasted over the
  inner margin, itself carrying 4 line-beginnings in a similar hand.
- No running title. Top margin blank.
- Tentative interpretation: a versified didactic text with section rubrics and a light
  apparatus of glosses and citations; the subject words that recur are "symon/symonis/symonia",
  "electio", "presul", "prelatus".

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Read: all 33 verse lines on each side, the red rubrics, and the legible glosses. Not fully
read: the cut left-margin glosses on side 2 and the pasted patch (only fragments), some faint
right-margin glosses on side 1.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Line label = image and line number counted from the top of that image; "p" numbers are my
running count of verse lines on the page. Overlaps: image-003 L1-3 repeat image-002 L7-9;
image-004 L1-3 repeat image-003 L14-16; image-007 L1-3 repeat image-006 L7-9; image-008 L1-3
repeat image-007 L14-16. Repeated lines are given once.

SIDE 1 (image-001 overview) - VERSE COLUMN
p1  image-002 L1:  Si maneat factum. n(on)? condicio. modo pactum
p2  image-002 L2:  Si t(ame)n occulta fiunt mercatio stulta.        [interlinear over the end: "symonie"; margin: "ut in p(re)allegata."]
p3  image-002 L3:  Ordinib(us) rite susceptis. si n(on)? symon.
p4  image-002 L4:  Vnu(m) (con)tulerit. michi p(re)sul dat pat(ri)moni(um)?   [interlinear over "Vnum": "ordinem"; margin: ".i. officiu(m). ita eni(m) ...? pat(er)? m[..]"]
p5  image-002 L5:  Exequor officium n(on)? presule restituente.
p6  image-002 L6:  Symonis eccl(esi)am si pura desero mente.        [margin: ".i. q. i. Sunt n(on)null(i)"]
p7  image-002 L7:  Tali corruptos q(uo)d ep(iscopu)s expiet ere.
p8  image-002 L8:  Saluo iudicio meliori credo licere.
p9  image-002 L9:  Tu t(ame)n assidue bona sic obtenta resigna.
p10 image-003 L4:  Peniteasq(ue) pri(us). scelus abstergens pi(et)ate? digna.   [margin: ".i. q. i. Sunt n(on)nulli. Ex / tra. Ex?. e. Mandato."]
p11 image-003 L5:  Dispensatoris t(ame)n inde sit omnib(us) horis:
p12 image-003 L6:  Intemerata man(us). alias metropolitanus.
p13 image-003 L7:  Iudicii libra. trutinet de pond(er)e rerum      [margin: "ut s(upra). C. p(ri)mo?. ...? / eu(m) ser? sequit(ur)?"]
p14 image-003 L8:  Tunc ea q(uo)d sua sit (et) dispensatio uerum
p15 image-003 L9:  Verba p(re)catiua. ueniunt q(ua)si munera queda(m)   [2-line initial V]
p16 image-003 L10: Symonis. indign(us) si sic intrauero. cedam     [margin: ".i. beneficiu(m) resignabo q(uia)? pec[..] / indigno."]
p17 image-003 L11: Sic faciam. si seruitio carnalit(er) acto       [interlinear over "Sic": "etiam"]
p18 image-003 L12: Me u(e)l in eccl(esi)e u(e)l in ordinis organa iacto
p19 image-003 L13: Si dign(us) fuero. p(re)ce carnis adepta tenebo.  [margin, below: ".i. p(er) ...iam? adep...? s(ed) n(on) teneor res[..]"]
p20 image-003 L14: S(ed) q(uod)? corrupta fuit hic intentio. flebo.
p21 image-003 L15: Si monachi. si canonici mundana p(er)osi        [2-line initial S]
p22 image-003 L16: Induerint habitu(m) reru(m) fetore leprosi.     [faint gloss at right: "p(re)ce? p(re)late?"]
p23 image-004 L3:  Si? scierint: cedant sinc(er)e. siue iubere?
p24 image-004 L4:  In cathedra soleant. loca u(e)l subiecta tene(re)
p25 image-004 L5:  Inq(ue) monasteriis ubi strictior ordo tenet(ur)
p26 image-004 L6:  Digne peniteant. donec lepra tota piet(ur).
p27 image-004 L7:  Talia sustineant. sup(er) hac q(ui)a? peste locuta.
p28 image-004 L8:  Concilii lat(er)anensis seuere statuta
p29 image-004 L9:  (Con)tempsere tam(en) q(ua)si uox sit friuola pape.
p30 image-004 L10: Q(uo)d tociens sit in hoc iuris transgressio. pape.   [left margin: "exclamatio"; right margin: "inuectio? ... / ponit. Sic. Mo...? ... / e. dama?. pape."]
p31 image-004 L11: At pri(us) ingressos (et) nota symonis arte.
p32 image-004 L12: Transfero. s(ed) mite modamine n(on) magis arte.
p33 image-004 L13: Si que p(er)cipi(un)t in co(m)moditate utentur   [last line; lower edge trims descenders]

SIDE 1 - RED RUBRICS, left margin (left edge cut)
image-003, beside p15-p17: [D]e hiis q(ui) p(er) p(re)ces / [..]iut? obseq(ui)a be- / [n]eficia (con)sequu(n)t(ur)
image-003/004, beside p21-p22: [D]e symonia / [c]laustraliu(m).

SIDE 2 (image-005 overview) - VERSE COLUMN
p1  image-006 L1:  Mansio (con)tinua fu(er)it deducta dierum
p2  image-006 L2:  Sic fiat noua p(er) alios electio demum         [gloss at end: "ut s(upra)."]
p3  image-006 L3:  Postq(uam) purgatum bene senserit ...a? iacentu(m)?   [second-last word unclear: "uiua"/"inua"?]
p4  image-006 L4:  Dispensare queat q(uod) casu p(re)sul in illo
p5  image-006 L5:  Siue monast(er)ium dico. n(on) mente uacillo.
p6  image-006 L6:  Q(uod)? n(on)? locu(m) gratis intrauit hec mea neptis.
p7  image-006 L7:  Seruio. sic facio de cunctis rite receptis.     [margin: "n(on)? fiat hec ex pact(i)o(n)e / p(re)cedenti. q(uia) t(un)c e(ss)et sy[..]"]
p8  image-006 L8:  Prelatu(m) uero cui symonis est data sedes.
p9  image-006 L9:  Q(u)is? ignaro. n(on) purgat presulis edes.     [margin: "q(uia) ad? ip(su)m ibit"]
p10 image-007 L4:  [C?]anonice cu(m) sis electus. mun(er)a nequam   [initial hidden by stain/patch]
p11 image-007 L5:  Erogat: inficiat ut causam nequit(er) eq(u)am?
p12 image-007 L6:  I(n)? tua sordescat electio. tu neq(ue) nosti.
p13 image-007 L7:  Nec (con)sensisti. gladius su(us) obuiet hosti
p14 image-007 L8:  Non t(e)?. se non te. uulpecula subdola uendit
p15 image-007 L9:  Te (con)firmabo. pereat qui rete tetendit       [mark "3"-like sign at end]
p16 image-007 L10: Emit(er)u(m)? ...sp(er)ni? adest. s(ed) amic(us) honore(m)   [first two words doubtful; faint gloss at right "qualis? ..."]
p17 image-007 L11: Ut tibi (con)quirat. tibi (com)parat ere fauore(m).
p18 image-007 L12: Dedicas. (et) te attollet? nulla uoluntas
p19 image-007 L13: Nec mun(us) ille man(us) p(ar)te? sic allicit unctas
p20 image-007 L14: Esto secur(us). no(n) est tibi tale uenenu(m).
p21 image-007 L15: Du(m)m(odo)? nil soluas. neq(ue) tunc n(ec)? postea c(er)tu(m).   [small gloss above end: illegible]
p22 image-007 L16: Presule cirsinato?. monachor(um) patre sacrato   [2-line initial P; second word as seen "cirſinato"/"ceſſinato"]
p23 image-008 L3:  Que tua su(n)t. scriptor. dapifer. pinc(er)na leuato
p24 image-008 L4:  Su(m)mopere studeas p(re)late reuolu(er)e tecu(m).
p25 image-008 L5:  Ne symon p(er) equu(m) u(e)l frenu(m) destruat equu(m).
p26 image-008 L6:  Symonis hic aut post. aut ante uolante sagitta.
p27 image-008 L7:  No(n) potit? secura cap(ut)? circu(m)dare uitta.
p28 image-008 L8:  Non potes absq(ue) nota p(re)lata sede potiri
p29 image-008 L9:  Si q(ua) sinistra tibi p(re)sumpt(i)o possit oriri.
p30 image-008 L10: (Con)dicio. pactu(m). u(e)l res extorta negetur.   [red strokes separating the three terms]
p31 image-008 L11: Quisq(ue) malu(m). sp(eci)emq(ue) mali. uitare iubet(ur)
p32 image-008 L12: Quid portas? su(m)mos cirsinales? redd(er)e porto   [2-line initial Q; "cirſinales" as seen]
p33 image-008 L13: Q(uo)d portas reru(m). n(on) xp̄i crescit in horto.

SIDE 2 - RED RUBRICS, right margin (right edge cut)
image-007, beside p10-p14: De duob(us) casib(us) / symonie. q(ui) no[n] / obsu(n)t electo u[..] / in benefician- / do.
image-007/008, beside p22-p24: De hiis q(ue) dant(ur) / i(n) (con)secr(ati)o(n)e pon[..] / ficu(m) u(e)l abbatu(m)
image-008, beside p32-p33: De nu(m)mis cir[..] / malib(us). (et) aliis [..]

SIDE 2 - left margin and pasted patch (fragments only)
image-006, beside p5: [..]nt participes sy. Ex.?
image-006/007, on the pasted patch beside p6-p9 (a different text, line-beginnings only):
   "...uota uo[..]" / "In melu[..]" / "In ueti? [..]" / "Res (con)iu[..]"
image-007/008, lower left margin (cut glosses): "[..]e. e. Sunt?" ; "[..]icit." ; "[..]cipes ..." ;
   "[..]udicet?" ; "[..]q(uo)d aliu[..]" ; "Obica[..]" ; "[..] mos erat? cu(m) n(on) erat." ;
   "[..]talia dant(ur)? ex pact(i)o(n)e / [..]sueta...? .i. q. i. ec?..."

4. LIMITATIONS
- The verse text is clear and mostly secure; the doubtful words are marked (side 1 p1/p3/p5 where
  a small "n" with superscript stroke is read "non" - it could be another n-abbreviation; p4 last
  word; p23; side 2 p3, p9 first word, p12 first letter, p16, p18 "attollet", p22 and p32
  "cirsin-" words, p27 "potit").
- Which side is recto is not determinable from the images; I have called them side 1 and side 2
  in packet order. Text does not obviously run on from the last line of side 1 to the first of
  side 2, nor the reverse; I have not tried to decide.
- Rubrics and marginal glosses are cut by the leaf edges; gaps left open. Marginal glosses are
  small and partly faint; readings there are approximate.
